children: European refiners will likely turn to West African, Mexican and Guyanese crude after Saudi Arabia reportedly cancelled October deliveries to Europe following damage to its East-West pipeline, according to Sparta Commodities' Aaron Kildow. However, replacement cargoes are unlikely to arrive before late October or early November. While Mexican and Guyanese crude also suits U.S. East Coast refiners, West African barrels currently offer better value into northwest Europe, meaning U.S. buyers might need to act quickly to secure enough supply, the analyst says.
